correctness.rationale: For W_n with n>=4 rim vertices and x=e^-t in (0,1), all distances are 0,1,2. Independently checked that rim block R=(1-x^4)I+(x-x^4)A_Cn+x^4 J has nonconstant Fourier eigenvalues 1-x^4+2(x-x^4)cos(2pi r/n); smallest is f_n=1-2c_n x+(2c_n-1)x^4. The hub–uniform-rim 2x2 sector has determinant g_n=1+2x+(n-3)x^4-nx^2=(1-x)[1+3x-(n-3)x^2(1+x)]. Their unique interior roots a_n and b_n follow from strict convexity of f and strict concavity of H. Exact independent rational checks of f even root alpha in (27/50,11/20), g8(11/20)>0, g9(27/50)<0, g7(63/100)>0 and f7(63/100)<0 (via rational cos lower bound) prove crossover at n=9 for all n, without exhaustive n sampling. Fourier multiplicities give nullity 2 for n=5,7 and 1 otherwise. The analytic implicit function calculation H_n(x)=0 yields x=n^-1/2+n^-1+n^-3/2+O(n^-2) and tau=(1/2)log n-n^-1/2-(1/2)n^-1+O(n^-3/2), while at n=3 K4 is PD for every t>0.

originality.rationale: Feragen–Lauze–Hauberg, Geodesic Exponential Kernels (arXiv:1411.0296), gives all-bandwidth positivity obstruction for continuous geodesic spaces, not a single bandwidth ray on a finite wheel vertex set. Lou–Obata–Huang arXiv:2001.06752 Example 3.6 derives wheel quadratic embedding constants for first-power graph distances; Obata 2017 independently studies the same unsquared QEC invariant. A nonnegative-type theorem for exp(-t d) for all t does not determine the threshold for exp(-t d^2). Resultary wheel-related matching titles concern wheel edge polytopes and unrelated matrices. No inspected stronger statement gives the exact order-nine mode switch; general diameter-two kernel matrix results remain a residual equivalence risk.
residual_risks: A general diameter-two three-level circulant-kernel theorem may include this finite-wheel root special case without explicit wheel wording.
The initial point t=0 is excluded: K(0)=J PSD but not PD; admissible classification is for t>0.
Finite eigenvalue experiments do not prove the all-n theorem.
